text:
Ryan Greene is in the part of a young center's season nobody puts on a poster. He hasn't had a point in ten games, and the Blackhawks just claimed Luke Glendening off waivers, a move The Athletic's Scott Powers said gives them flexibility "to move Ryan Greene around." Chicago is last in the league in faceoffs, and Greene is one of four young centers learning that part of the job at once.

The dip is partly real. His chances have dried up over the last ten games, and at five on five Chicago has taken 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on. But the finish has been cruel: the Blackhawks have scored 7.8 fewer goals than those chances deserve with him on the ice, a gap that usually closes. There's a useful player under it, too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 69% of his zone exits leaving with possession last season, and Evolving-Hockey noted he played with some of the weakest linemates in the league. Forwards drafted where he was typically score about 0.29 points a game in their first full season; he's at 0.17 through 24.
headline: Ryan Greene's growing pains down the middle
